proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(Z=(y,M,B,s_1)\), with both matrices vectorized in a fixed order, and let \(\widehat Z=(\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives the joint expansion over the fixed collection of cells and coordinates
\[
 \widehat Z-Z=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i+r_K,
 \qquad \sqrt K\,\|r_K\|_2\longrightarrow_P0.
\]
Every cell influence vector is centered by the definition of \(\phi_c\).  Assumptions~\ref{ass:cell-iid} and~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} therefore make the stacked vectors \(\Phi_1,\ldots,\Phi_K\) independent and identically distributed with mean zero.  Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment}, finiteness of \(\mathcal C\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel} imply
\[
 E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2<\infty.
\]
Independence and centering give
\[
 E\left\|K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_i\right\|_2^2
 =E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2.
\]
Markov's inequality applied to the squared norm shows that the normalized sum is \(O_P(1)\).  It follows from the first display that
\[
 \|\widehat Z-Z\|_2=O_P(K^{-1/2}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat M-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]

Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank} gives \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:singular-gap} gives \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa>0\).  Therefore \(M_r=M\) and \(P=M^+\).  Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} supplies a neighborhood of \((y,M,B)\) on which \(\mathcal F(y,M,B)=yM_r^+B\) is Fr\'echet differentiable with the displayed full derivative.  Since \(\widehat Z\to_PZ\), the probability that \(\widehat Z\) lies in this neighborhood tends to one.  The definition of Fr\'echet differentiability, the preceding \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\) bound, Definition~\ref{def:full-spectral-map}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:full-spectral-differential} consequently give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\theta-\theta
 &=(\widehat y-y)PB
   +y\mathcal L_M(\widehat M-M)B
   +yP(\widehat B-B)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
   \left\{\Phi_{y,i}PB+y\mathcal L_M(\Phi_{M,i})B
                 +yP\Phi_{B,i}\right\}
   +o_P(K^{-1/2})\\
 &=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\theta,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The factual-post block of Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} is
\[
 \widehat s_1-s_1
 =K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{1,i}+o_P(K^{-1/2}).
\]
Stacking the last two displays and applying Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} proves the asserted asymptotic linear representation
\[
 \sqrt K
 \begin{pmatrix}\widehat\theta-\theta\\ \widehat s_1-s_1\end{pmatrix}
 =K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}+o_P(1).
\]

We next derive the Gaussian limit.  Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence} is a fixed linear map from \(\Phi_i\) to \(\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  Its coefficients are finite because \(\sigma_r(M)\ge\kappa>0\) implies \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\kappa^{-1}\), while \(y\), \(M\), and \(B\) are finite-dimensional matrices.  Hence Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} yields
\[
 E\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^{2+\nu}<\infty,
 \qquad E\Phi_{\eta,i}=0,
 \qquad E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta.
\]
Fix \(a\in\mathbb R^{2J}\), put \(W_i=a^\top\Phi_{\eta,i}\), and set \(\delta=\min(\nu,1)>0\).  The elementary Taylor remainder bound
\[
 \left|e^{\mathrm ix}-1-\mathrm ix+\frac{x^2}{2}\right|
 \le C_\delta |x|^{2+\delta},\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
follows from the third-order Taylor formula when \(|x|\le1\) and from \(1+|x|+x^2/2\le(5/2)|x|^{2+\delta}\) when \(|x|>1\).  Therefore, with \(\omega_a^2=a^\top\Omega_\eta a\),
\[
 \left|E e^{\mathrm iW_i/\sqrt K}
       -1+\frac{\omega_a^2}{2K}\right|
 \le C_\delta K^{-1-\delta/2}E|W_i|^{2+\delta}
 =o(K^{-1}).
\]
Raising this characteristic function to the \(K\)-th power gives
\[
 E\exp\!\left\{\mathrm i a^\top K^{-1/2}
             \sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\right\}
 \longrightarrow \exp(-\omega_a^2/2).
\]
The limit is the characteristic function of \(\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta)\); the continuity criterion for characteristic functions therefore yields
\[
 K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N_{2J}(0,\Omega_\eta).
\]
Together with the asymptotic linear representation, this proves the displayed limit law.  Assumption~\ref{ass:nondegenerate-covariance} gives \(a^\top\Omega_\eta a\ge v\|a\|_2^2\), so the limiting Gaussian law is nondegenerate.

It remains to prove consistency of the fitted influence vectors and covariance.  We first justify every spectral substitution.  For a matrix \(A\) near \(M\), let \(\Pi_R(A)\) be the orthogonal projector onto its leading \(r\) right singular subspace.  The variational characterization of singular values and
\[
 \bigl|\|Ax\|_2-\|Mx\|_2\bigr|
 \le\|(A-M)x\|_2\le\|A-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|x\|_2
\]
imply \(|\sigma_j(A)-\sigma_j(M)|\le\|A-M\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) for every \(j\).  The exact-rank and singular-gap assumptions thus make the leading \(r\)-dimensional subspace unique throughout a sufficiently small neighborhood of \(M\).  To see its continuity, note that rank-\(r\) orthogonal projectors form a compact set and that \(\Pi_R(A)\) maximizes
\[
 Q\longmapsto\operatorname{tr}(QA^\top A)
\]
over that set.  If \(A_m\to M\), every convergent subsequence of \(\Pi_R(A_m)\) must therefore maximize \(Q\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(QM^\top M)\).  The fixed gap makes the latter maximizer uniquely equal to \(\Pi_R(M)\).  Hence
\[
 \Pi_R(A)\longrightarrow\Pi_R(M),
 \qquad A_r=A\Pi_R(A)\longrightarrow M.
\]
On this neighborhood the identity
\[
 A_r^+=\left\{A_r^\top A_r+I-\Pi_R(A)\right\}^{-1}A_r^\top
\]
is verified directly in a singular-vector basis; the matrix inside braces has eigenvalues \(\sigma_1(A)^2,\ldots,\sigma_r(A)^2,1,\ldots,1\), all bounded away from zero locally.  Matrix multiplication and inversion are continuous there, so
\[
 (\widehat M)_r^+\longrightarrow_P P.
\]
Substitution into the explicit formula in Definition~\ref{def:full-differential} now gives, in operator norm on the finite-dimensional space of matrix perturbations,
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\longrightarrow_P\mathcal L_M.
\]

Let \(\widehat\Phi_i\) denote the stack of fold-specific fitted cell influence vectors.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion} gives their foldwise \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency.  Conditional on each training sample, the mean validation-fold squared error has conditional expectation equal to that \(L_2(P_c)\) error.  Conditional Markov inequalities, followed by the finite union bound over the fixed cells and folds, therefore give
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2=o_P(1).
\]
Let \(\mathsf A\) be the fixed linear operator in Definition~\ref{def:transported-influence}, including the unchanged factual-post block, and let \(\widehat{\mathsf A}\) be its plug-in version.  The convergence of \(\widehat y\), \(\widehat M\), \(\widehat B\), \((\widehat M)_r^+\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_{\widehat M}\) proves
\[
 \|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_P(1),
 \qquad \|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_P(1).
\]
Moreover, \(K^{-1}\sum_i\|\Phi_i\|_2^2=O_P(1)\) by Markov's inequality and \(E\|\Phi_i\|_2^2<\infty\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K
 \|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2
 &\le 2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
       K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_i-\Phi_i\|_2^2\\
 &\quad+2\|\widehat{\mathsf A}-\mathsf A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
       K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\Phi_i\|_2^2
 =o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
This is the claimed empirical \(L_2\) consistency.

Set \(D_i=\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}-\Phi_{\eta,i}\).  Expanding the difference of outer products and applying Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\left\|\widehat\Omega_\eta-
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &\quad\le
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|D_i\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \left[
 \left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\widehat\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 +\left\{K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\|\Phi_{\eta,i}\|_2^2\right\}^{1/2}
 \right]
 =o_P(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
For any two coordinates \(k,m\), the product
\(\Phi_{\eta,i,k}\Phi_{\eta,i,m}\) is integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz.  Truncate this product at a fixed level, apply Chebyshev's inequality to the resulting bounded independent variables, and then let the truncation level tend to infinity.  This proves the entrywise weak law; because \(2J\) is fixed,
\[
 K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top
 \longrightarrow_P E(\Phi_{\eta,i}\Phi_{\eta,i}^\top)=\Omega_\eta.
\]
Combining the last two displays proves \(\widehat\Omega_\eta\to_P\Omega_\eta\).

Finally, the observed-law map and the causal target must be kept distinct.  Lemma~\ref{lem:joint-cell-expansion}, using Assumptions~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring} and~\ref{ass:censor-positivity}, centers every AIPCW cell coordinate at the covariate-standardized event survival \(S_c(t)=E\{Q_c(t\mid X_{ci})\}\), so \(y\), \(M\), \(B\), and \(s_1\) are observed-law identified survival blocks rather than marginal Kaplan--Meier pseudo-targets.  Assumption~\ref{ass:target-pre-span} supplies the donor-row representation of \(y\).  Separately, Assumption~\ref{ass:post-transport} states that the target unit's untreated post-treatment survival row equals the observed-law functional \(yM_r^+B\).  Only this last identifying restriction establishes the equality between that functional and the causal curve \(\theta\).  Thus the limit law is centered at the untreated counterfactual curve, while \(s_1\) remains the factual treated curve, completing the proof.

added_lemmas.statement:
On the fixed pre- and post-treatment grids, suppose the latent-factor restrictions used by Han and Shah~\cite{HanShah2025SSC}, Theorems~1--2 and Appendix~E, can be written
\[
 M=VU_0,\qquad y=v_n^\top U_0,\qquad B=VU_1,
\]
where \(V\in\mathbb R^{N_0\times d}\), \(U_0\in\mathbb R^{d\times T_0}\), \(U_1\in\mathbb R^{d\times J}\), and \(v_n\in\mathbb R^d\).  Write their unit-factor-span condition as \(v_n^\top=w^\top V\) for some \(w\in\mathbb R^{N_0}\), and their post/pre time-factor-span condition as \(U_1=U_0A\) for some \(A\in\mathbb R^{T_0\times J}\).  If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), then
\[
 y\in\operatorname{row}(M),\qquad
 yM_r^+B=yA=v_n^\top U_1.
\]
Thus the observed-law spectral functional equals the latent untreated target-post grid on this fixed-grid subclass.  Moreover, the rational law \(P^\star\) in Definition~\ref{def:rational-witness} satisfies these factor/span restrictions by taking \(d=2\), \(V=I_2\), \(U_0=M\), \(U_1=B\), \(A=M^{-1}B\), and \(v_n^\top=yM^{-1}\); for that law the common value is \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The unit-factor-span condition and the three factorization identities give, equation by equation,
\[
 y=v_n^\top U_0=w^\top VU_0=w^\top M.
\]
Hence \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\), which proves the first conclusion.  By Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank}, \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), so the rank-\(r\) truncation of \(M\) is \(M\) itself and \(M_r^+=M^+\).

To verify the projector identity needed below rather than assume it, take a thin singular-value decomposition \(M=U\Sigma R^\top\), where \(U^\top U=R^\top R=I_r\) and every diagonal entry of \(\Sigma\) is positive.  Then
\[
 M^+=R\Sigma^{-1}U^\top,
 \qquad M^+M=RR^\top.
\]
Because \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)=\operatorname{row}(R^\top)\), there is a row \(b^\top\in\mathbb R^{1\times r}\) such that \(y=b^\top R^\top\).  Consequently,
\[
 yM^+M=b^\top R^\top RR^\top=b^\top R^\top=y.
\]
The post/pre time-factor-span condition now yields
\[
 B=VU_1=VU_0A=MA.
\]
Combining the last two displays gives
\[
 yM_r^+B=yM^+MA=yA
   =v_n^\top U_0A=v_n^\top U_1,
\]
which proves the fixed-grid embedding.  Notice that the equality to the latent untreated post grid follows from the displayed factor and span restrictions; it is not created by defining the observed-law functional.

For the final assertion, Definition~\ref{def:rational-witness} gives
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}4/5&3/5\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 y=(7/10,9/20),
 \qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Direct calculation gives
\[
 \det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35=-\frac3{25}\ne0,
 \qquad yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2).
\]
Thus \(M\) has rank two.  With \(V=I_2\), \(U_0=M\), \(U_1=B\), \(A=M^{-1}B\), and \(v_n^\top=yM^{-1}\), one has
\[
 VU_0=M,\qquad v_n^\top U_0=y,
 \qquad VU_1=B,
 \qquad U_0A=MM^{-1}B=B=U_1,
\]
and the unit-factor span holds with \(w=v_n\).  Finally,
\[
 v_n^\top U_1=(1/2,1/2)
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
 =(3/5,3/10)=\theta.
\]
This proves that the witness belongs to the same fixed-grid factor/span subclass.
added_lemmas.justification: The proposition embeds Han and Shah's fixed-grid latent-factor conditions into the row-space and exact-transport restrictions used by the spectral theorem, rather than merely asserting that the two setups coincide.
added_lemmas.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) provide the factor and PCR architecture; the proposition records the exact matrix bridge to the row-donor orientation used here and verifies that the rational Kaplan--Meier/PCR witness remains inside that structural subclass.
added_lemmas.consumer: The bridge shows that the fixed-grid theorem targets the untreated United States post-treatment survival curve in the 925-patient, 10-country TCL analysis whenever the stated Han--Shah spans hold.

proposed.comparator_claim: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) impose event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, use a fixed-grid latent-factor/PCR transport, and form the spectral inputs from marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves; they do not derive covariate-adjusted AIPCW spectral influence inference.
Theorem 2 gives pointwise and uniform asymptotic linearity for one cross-fitted doubly robust treatment-specific survival curve.
Theorem 2 and Corollary 2 give row-space out-of-sample prediction guarantees for minimum-norm principal component regression.
Equation (4.12) gives the Fr\'echet derivative of the Moore--Penrose inverse under locally constant rank.
Sections 3--4 show interpolation, variance, and survival-curve bias for synthetic survival individuals.
Theorem 3.1 gives feasible inference for low-rank linear functionals when the working rank overestimates the true rank.

Theorem 2.1 recovers the factor space for bounded working rank at least the true rank as the cross-sectional dimension grows, and Theorem 3.2 with Corollary 3.1 gives over-estimated-rank-robust factor-augmented inference.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The Han--Shah comparator row incorrectly described their premise as non-informative censoring. Their stated condition is conditional independence given treatment and covariates; the distinction is that their spectral inputs are marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves, whereas this note uses covariate-adjusted AIPCW inputs and transports their full influence law.

prose_updates.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, rank, and a separated nonzero singular spectrum, covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates admit a joint root-\(K\) expansion under censor positivity, a nuisance product rate, and explicit bounded-variation and variation-rate restrictions on the fitted relative-survival paths. Differentiating the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks yields the full spectral influence vector, consistent covariance estimation, fixed-grid simultaneous bands, and a studentized grid-RMST interval. A matrix embedding shows that Han and Shah's unit-factor and time-factor spans imply the row-space and post-transport conditions used here, and the rational Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias witness lies in that fixed-grid factor subclass. Han and Shah already assume conditional independent censoring given treatment and covariates; the advance is covariate adjustment of their marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier step when covariate heterogeneity induces marginal dependent censoring. The weak-gap and selected-rank frontier remains open.

project_justification.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) already state event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates, but their spectral workflow uses marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier curves and does not give a covariate-adjusted joint influence law. With heterogeneous covariates, conditional independence need not imply marginal independence, so those cell inputs can converge to distorted curves before PCR transport. Westling et al. (2024, Theorem 2) provide orthogonal survival-score theory for a directly estimated treatment-specific curve, not for a learned three-block spectral counterfactual.
project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), the covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage and the counterfactual is a smooth spectral functional only on a separated-rank neighborhood. The needed bridge combines an exact Stieltjes remainder under disclosed learner-path variation control, all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative, and an algebraic embedding of Han--Shah's fixed-grid factor spans.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the repaired AIPCW cell expansion, the joint transported Gaussian law with consistently estimated influence vectors and covariance, a Gaussian-multiplier simultaneous band, and a studentized grid-RMST interval. It also proves a relatively open conditional-censoring subclass on which unadjusted marginal Kaplan--Meier/PCR has fixed bias, using an explicit rational witness that remains inside the Han--Shah factor/span subclass.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) supply the fixed-grid latent-factor survival panel, unit and time spans, PCR transport, and the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application. They already assume event-time/censoring conditional independence given treatment and covariates; the present advance is therefore not a weaker censoring premise, but replacement of marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier inputs by covariate-adjusted AIPCW inputs when within-cell covariate heterogeneity creates marginal dependent censoring, together with full transported inference. Proposition~\ref{prop:han-shah-fixed-grid-embedding} gives the exact matrix bridge from their spans to \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\) and \(yM_r^+B\), while Proposition~\ref{prop:km-pcr-cancellation} certifies an open class of fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024, Theorem 2 and Sections 5.2--5.3) supply the cross-fitted augmented survival-score architecture and direct-curve inference, but not a data-dependent spectral transport; the substantive relative-survival variation condition imposed here is stronger than their ordinary product-rate bookkeeping. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025, Theorem 2 and Corollary 2) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space prediction without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973, equation (4.12)) are the matrix-calculus ancestor for the constant-rank pseudoinverse derivative. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024, Sections 3--4) analyze survival synthetic-control bias but do not derive this three-block PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) and Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2026) address growing-panel or rank-robust factor inference rather than the fixed-dimension separated-rank theorem proved here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results cover only the fixed-panel, fixed-grid, exact-rank, fixed-singular-gap, exact-span, and exact-post-transport subclass. They additionally require conditional independent censoring, a common positive censor-survival bound, nondegenerate transported covariance, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, event-origin normalization, and the substantive bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions on fitted relative-survival paths. The joint-cell lemma is now proved under those restrictions; it is no longer an open premise, and the spectral limit, fixed-grid band, and grid-RMST interval inherit the restrictions transitively. The Han--Shah embedding is algebraic and does not establish those censoring, covariance, or learner conditions. The rational \(2\times2\) witness belongs to the fixed-grid factor/span subclass, while its negative Kaplan--Meier/PCR conclusion does not require the positive theorem's learner assumptions. Nothing here covers growing donor or time dimensions, a growing post grid, a shrinking or closed singular gap, selected rank, covariance degeneracy, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. The weak-gap and rank-selection problem remains the clear tier-changing follow-up, so the present contribution is a solid specialized fixed-grid result rather than a flagship general theory.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem supplies a joint root-\(K\) law and consistently estimable covariance for the covariate-adjusted spectral untreated curve and its factual comparator, including perturbations from the target-pre, donor-pre, and donor-post blocks.
statement_notes.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) assume conditional independent censoring given treatment and covariates but analyze marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier/PCR inputs; Westling et al. (2024, Theorem 2) analyze a directly estimated covariate-adjusted survival curve without learned spectral transport. Neither gives this full three-block influence vector or its joint covariance law.
statement_notes.consumer: The theorem provides standard errors for the untreated United States curve and its contrast with observed single-agent therapy in the 925-patient, 10-country TCL analysis.
